title: The naive framing: "Claude learned a new skill"
text: You guess Claude learned a new trick called build guide. It didn't. It was handed a file of instructions. Build guide just names one such file. Let's see what's actually inside it. Here

title: Sounds like an upgrade
text: Claude has a new skill and it sounds like an upgrade, like it studied and came back knowing something it didn't before.

title: Broken, with a case — delete the folder, nothing is forgotten
text: But nothing in the model changes. Delete the skills folder and Claude doesn't forget anything. There was nothing to learn. It just stops following that one routine.

title: The anchor: one file — build-guide's single SKILL.md
text: Here's what a skill actually is, one file. Build guide, for instance, is a folder holding a single skill. MD, the whole routine written in plain language Claude reads before it starts. Claude

title: Read it, then follow it in order
text: Reads that file top to bottom and works through it step by step in the order it's written, no branching unless the file itself says branch. That makes a

title: Spec, not power — the payoff and the limit
text: Skill a specification, not a new power. The payoff, repeatable results run after run. The limit, anything outside those written steps and Claude is off the map.

title: The anchor returns — same file, every run
text: So build guide never taught Claude anything new. It just guarantees that every time build guide runs, Claude reads that same file and works through the same steps. That's the whole trick.

title: Both directions — neither one is proof
text: Watching Claude follow the file exactly doesn't prove the routine is good. A bad process can be followed to the letter and watching it improvise doesn't prove the skill is broken. It may just be a case the file never covered. A skill

title: Carry-out
text: Doesn't teach Claude something new. It's a file of steps Claude reads before it starts, so the same request gets the same routine every time.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Pick one task I repeat the same way every time. Write me a skill MD for it, plain language ordered steps, then read it back to me and walk me through exactly what you'll do before you do it. Claude
